reason: The cited evidence (E1) directly supports the first three premises by showing that atomic-scale compositional fluctuations in CoCrFeNi nanopillars cause SFE variations, which coordinate twinning and slip to achieve ~110% uniform elongation and high flow stress. However, the hypothesis extends this mechanism to bulk samples with controlled grain size and texture, a condition not addressed in E1, which used single-crystalline nanopillars. The fourth premise thus lacks direct support, and the translation to bulk behavior is an overstatement relative to the cited evidence.
premises: Chemical heterogeneity in HEAs causes local variations in stacking fault energy (SFE)
Local SFE variations enable synergistic activation of deformation twinning and dislocation slip
Twin-dislocation interactions delay strain localization and necking
Controlling grain size and texture isolates the effect of chemical heterogeneity on mechanical behavior
The proposed mechanism leads to enhanced uniform elongation and high flow stress
